items.finding: The source notes that the temperature sensitivity of OH bands poses a significant drawback for measuring aqueous solutions using infrared spectroscopy.
items.how_it_applies: This highlights the necessity of monitoring or controlling temperature when acquiring spectra in aqueous media to account for potential spectral shifts.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The finding stems from a review of downstream processing and may not directly reflect the thermal conditions in an upstream cell culture.

citation.quote: Additionally, the temperature sensitivity of the OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR, which makes tempered sample holders necessary [29].
citation.label: E01 ¶12

items.finding: Low-level data fusion rearranges data from different sources into a new matrix where variables are placed sequentially.
items.how_it_applies: This supports structuring low-level data combination by concatenating variable blocks from different spectroscopic methods for subsequent modeling.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The literature source discusses general PAT applications, so the specific matrix and analytical methods must be tested for cell culture monitoring.

citation.quote: Low-level data fusion (LLDF) is considered the simplest method to achieve a combination of inputs. In this case, the data is rearranged into a new data matrix, where the variables coming from different sources are placed one after the other.
citation.label: E02 ¶31
